summary: Flathead National Forest patrol lookout 2.5 miles south of Sanders Mountain; camp set up in 1930 and abandoned in 1948 per Kemnow.

facts.status_note: Kemnow's entry gives 1948 as the abandonment year, citing Kresek; no later source found for the site

events.note: July 7, 1930 Daily Inter Lake report, quoted by Kemnow: a pack string went into Grubb Mountain in Pleasant Valley to establish camp for a lookout
Kemnow's entry reads '1948: Abandoned.' citing Kresek. The Sanders Mountain page also says 'Abandoned 1948. Gone.' but does not say which site it means

evidence.supports: Forest is the Flathead National Forest
Patrol lookout 2.5 miles south of Sanders Mountain
evidence.quote: A patrol lookout 2 1/2 miles south of Sanders Mountain L.O. (Kresek)

evidence.supports: 1930 pack string to establish camp for a lookout
evidence.quote: A pack string has gone in to Grubb Mountain in Pleasant valley today to establish camp for a lookout

evidence.supports: Setting up the camp completed the lookout and smoke-chaser system in the Kalispell district
evidence.quote: which completes the association system of lookouts and smoke chasers in the Kalispell district

evidence.supports: Sanders Mountain tower: 50-foot metal tower and cabin, dated 1934
Patrol 2.5 miles south on Grubb Mountain
evidence.quote: Patrol 2.5 miles south on Grubb Mtn.

evidence.supports: Sanders page says Abandoned 1948 and Gone
Agency is the Flathead National Forest

notes_for_editor: Two web pages only. Kemnow's entry is the sole source for the 1930 camp and the 1948 abandonment, and it relays both from a newspaper and from a source named Kresek. The Sanders page says 'Abandoned 1948. Gone.' for the Sanders tower's record, which may or may not refer to the Grubb patrol; the story says so. No source describes the site today, and access is unknown. Location and agency agree across both sources.
